questions.question: Which of the following techniques can be used to separate the impurities in Milk?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Column chromatography**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Column Chromatography**

 
 
• The **separation and purification of substances from a solution to obtain the simpler substances from the complex elements is called column chromatography**.
 
• The process of separation employs **five different types of column chromatography**.
 
• The** two phases** of the procedure are the **mobile phase and the stationary phase**. 
 
• In this **solid-liquid method**, the **stationary phase is a solid** and the **mobile phase is a liquid or gas**.
 
• Applications of **Column Chromatography**
 
 
• **separation of** a complex mixture.
 
• **purification** or the process of** removing impurities**.
 
• isolation of the **active elements**.
 
• **removing metabolites **from bodily fluids.
 
• **estimation **of pharmaceutical compounds or crude extracts.
 
• Column Chromatography can also be used to **separate the impurities in Milk**.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microscopy**

 
 
• The** method of viewing things that are invisible to the naked eye is called microscopy**.
 
• ​The **range** can be any value between** mm and nm**.
 
• **Optical microscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and electron microscopy **are the three main microscopic techniques that are used.
 
 
 
• **Microtomy**
 
 
• **Microtomy **is a technique that can be used instead of electropolishing and ion milling **to prepare thin sections for materials like bones, minerals, and teeth**.
 
• The **section thickness of a microtome** can be adjusted to be between** 50 nm and 100 m, thin enough to divide a human hair across its breadth**.
 
 
 
• **Autoclave**
 
 
• An **autoclave is a device used to perform industrial and scientific procedures **that demand for **higher pressure and/or temperature** than ambient conditions.
 
• To **eliminate dangerous germs, viruses, fungus, and spores on objects inside a pressure vessel, steam is used under pressure in this machine**.

questions.question: The Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) scheme, which was launched in ________________ 2021, aims at facilitating the academic mobility of students, giving them the freedom to study across the higher educational institutions in India with the help of a ‘credit scheme’ mechanism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**July**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Academic Bank of Credit (ABC)**

 
 
• The Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) scheme, which was launched in** July 2021**, aims at facilitating the **academic mobility of students, giving them the freedom to study across the higher educational institutions in India with the help of a ‘credit scheme’ mechanism**.
 
• The** National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** of the **Government of India** originally envisioned it as a **loan facility**.
 
• The ABC will be in charge of tasks including** opening, closing, and validating each student's individual academic account**.
 
• Additionally, it will be in charge of collecting the a**cademic credits that students have earned from their different higher education institutions, validating them, storing them, transferring or redeeming them, and disseminating them among its stakeholders** as and when necessary.
 
• The programme will cover all types of **graduate-level, postgraduate, PhD, diploma, certificate, and other courses **given by higher education institutions that are approved by the** University Grants Commission (UGC)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **ABC of India** will require students to **manually open an account**, followed by ABC's standard operating rules, and **provide a special ID that may be used to identify each student's account with the ABC**.
 
• Over** 290 of the best higher education institutions** in India** will join the bank** when it begins operations in the academic year **2021–2022**.
 
• All of the institutions that rank among the** top 100 according to the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) and all of the institutions that have received National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) "Grade A" **accreditation will be included in this group.
 
• Additionally,** SWAYAM, NPTEL, V-Lab, and other programmes** that provide their courses are qualified to use the services **offered by Academic Bank of Credit**.

questions.question: How many Primary Health Centres are there in rural areas of India as per 31st March 2020 data?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30813**__.

__
 
• **Primary Health Centres (PHCs)**

 
 
• The **fundamental structural and operational component of public health services **in developing nations is the **Primary Healthcare Center (PHC)**.
 
• PHCs were **created to provide people with primary healthcare that is easily accessible, reasonably priced, and readily available**, in accordance with the **Alma Ata Declaration of 1978 by the World Health Organization (WHO) **member countries.
 
• Primary Health Centers (PHC) are established** under the National Health Mission (NHM)** to serve** 20,000 people in mountainous, tribal, and desert areas** and** 30,000 **people in **rural areas**.
 
• According to the **Rural Health Statistics 2019–20**, there were** 5,895 urban PHCs** and** 30,813 rural PHCs** operating in the nation as of March 31, 2020.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PHCs** are the** principal first-line** providers of** primary healthcare in South Asia**.
 
• For outreach services including **immunisation, basic curative treatment, maternity and child health services, and preventative services, each PHC has five or six sub-centres staffed by health workers**.
 
• There are currently** 23,109 PHCs in India**.
 
• **National Health Mission**
 
 
• Under the **National Health Mission (NHM)**, States are given financial assistance to improve their p**ublic health systems, notably by building new or upgrading existing facilities**.
 
• **Infrastructure spending** is allowed under **NHM in high-priority states for up to 33 per cent** and in **other States up to 25 per cent**.

questions.question: In a resistor, what happens to the current when the resistance is doubled?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The current gets halved.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The obstruction to current flow is electrical resistance**.
 
• This implies that when r**esistance is lower, current will be higher**.
 
• **Ohm's Law** states that the **current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V)** across it.
 
• ** V = I R**, where **R **is the conductor's** resistance**
 
• It can also be written as ,
 
• ** I = V/R,**
 
• This means that if **resistance doubles, current will decrease by half because current and resistance have an inverse relationship**.
 
• SI unit of resistance is **Ohm (****Ω)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistor**

 
 
• A **resistor is a passive electrical component having two terminals that control or limits the passage of electric current in electrical circuits**.
 
• Resistors come in a **variety of sizes and forms**.
 
• There are two popular types: **through-hole and surface mount**.
 
• A resistor might be **static, conventional, unique, or part of a set of variable resistors**.
 
 
 
• **Application of Resistor**
 
 
• When a**ccurate measurement, high sensitivity, and balanced current regulation are needed**, wire wound resistors are used in applications like shunt with ampere metres.
 
• **Flame detectors, burglar alarms, photographic equipment**, etc. all use photoresistors.
 
• **Temperature and voltmeter control** is accomplished by resistors.
 
• **Amplifiers, telephony, oscillators, and digital multimeters** all use resistors.
 
• Additionally, they are utilised in** transmitters, demodulators, and modulators**.

• **Arjuna's Penance**

 
 
• A monument called **Descent of the Ganges, also referred to as Arjuna's Penance** locally may be found in the** Indian state of Tamil Nadu's Chengalpattu district in Mamallapuram **on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Arjuna’s Penance, **a mammoth architecture with finely carved rock sculptures, serves as a venue for the Mamallapuram Dance Festival, in the backdrop of the Bay of Bengal**.
 
• It is a massive **open-air rock relief that is 96 by 43 feet (29 by 13 metres) in size** and carved onto **two monolithic rock boulders**.

• The relief was made to commemorate **Narasimhavarman I's victory over Chalukya monarch Pulakesin II**.
 
• The area, presently referred to as Mamallapuram, **was formerly known by the nickname Mamallan, the "great wrestler" or "great warrior,"** given to **King Narasimhavarman I of the Pallava Dynasty**.
 
• He ruled from the **4th to the 9th centuries, from 630-668 AD**.

questions.question: _______ of the Constitution deals with the amendment procedure of the Constitution.

__
 
• **Article 368**

 
 
• **Amending India's Constitution** involves altering the** fundamental or ultimate law of the country**.
 
• **Part XX (Article 368) of the Indian Constitution **specifies the process for** amending the constitution**.
 
• This process **protects the Constitution of India's sanctity and restrains the Parliament of India's arbitrary power**.
 
• The** 24th and 42nd Amendments, passed in 1971 and 1976**, respectively, amended **Article 368**.
 
• As stated in **Part-xx Article 368 (1) of the Indian Constitution**, Parliament may alter the Constitution by **adding to, changing, or repealing any provision in accordance with the procedure specified therein**, which is distinct from the procedure for ordinary modifications.
 
• According to the process **outlined in article 368 for amending the Constitution, a change can only be made by introducing a Bill in one of the two Houses of Parliament**.

questions.question: ________ zone is generally defined as an environment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters.

The correct answer is __**Temperate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperate Zone**

 
 
• Between the** tropics and the polar regions** is where the t**emperate zone primarily exists**.
 
• There are typically **four distinct seasons**, with a **vast variation in temperatures and precipitation**.
 
• It is generally defined as an e**nvironment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters**. 
 
• The** continental United States, the majority of Canada and Europe, Central Asia, southern South America, and southern Australia** are among the areas that are exclusively covered in the **temperate zone**.
 
• The average temperature of the temperate zone lies between zero and 20°C.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Zone**

 
 
• The areas of the** planet closest to the equator and between the Tropics of Cancer in the north and Capricorn in the south are known as tropical regions**.
 
• The average temperature in the tropics ranges from **25 to 28 degrees Celsius (77 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit)**.
 
 
 
• **Dry Zone**
 
 
• The** sub-humid regions of the nation that receive 75 cm to 100 cm of rainfall **(and hence have moisture deficiency for two-thirds of the year) and the** semi-arid regions that receive 30 cm to 75 cm of rainfall are considered dry-land zones**.
 
 
 
• **Continental Zone**
 
 
• The region with the** largest geographic scope is known as the Continental Zone (CON)**, which also encompasses portions of the** lower hills on the ALS border as well as the plains and lowlands of Central and Eastern Europe and the Balkans**.
 
• The weather is continental, with** wide annual temperature variations and heavy summertime precipitation**.

questions.question: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar 2021, for the identification and nurturing of budding and young talent, was given to ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manav Rachna Educational Institution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar**

 
 
• An honour given by the Republic of **India in sports is the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar**.
 
• The** Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** bestows it annually.
 
• The award honours** "corporates, nonprofits, and sports control boards' role in the promotion and growth of sports in the nation"** over the previous three years.
 
• The award was** launched in 2009, and in 2015, the rules were updated**. 
 
• Since the modification, organisations are awarded in the following four categories: **sports for development, Identification and nurturing of budding and young talent, corporate social responsibility initiatives to promote sports and employment of athletes, and sports welfare programs**.
 
• The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar 2021, for the identification and nurturing of budding and young talent, was given to **M**anav Rachna Educational Institution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Sports Promotion Award **is the translation of the award's name into Hindi.
 
• The award was presented to Manav Rachna Educational Institution by the **Hon. Ram Nath Kovind, the former President of India in 2021**.
 
• The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar 2021,** for the encouragement ****of sports through corporate social responsibility, was given to Oil and Natural Gas Corporation.**
 
• The award is **presented annually at the Presidential Palace by the President of India**, usually on** August 29th of each year**, together with the other **five National Sports Awards and the National Adventure Award**.

questions.question: Which Indian shuttler defeated World Champion Loh Kean Yew of Singapore in the Men's Singles final at the 2022 India Open?

__

• In the **men's singles final of the India Open 2022, Indian badminton player Lakshya Sen defeated Singaporean World Champion Loh Kean Yew**.
 
• He won his **first Super 500 championship**.

• The **Yonex-Sunrise India Open 2022**, also known as the **2022 India Open (badminton), took place at the K. D. Jadhav Indoor Hall in New Delhi, India**.

• **Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy** defeat** Mohammad Ahsan and Hendra Setiawan of Indonesia** to win the Indian Open for the first time in Men's Double.
 
• In **43 minutes**, Satwik and Chirag defeated the Indonesian pair ranked No. 2 in the world by a **score of 21-16, 26-24**.

• **Indian badminton player Srikanth Kidambi **receives his training at the **Gopichand Badminton Academy in Hyderabad**.

questions.question: Identify the method that is NOT used to purify organic compounds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sedimentation**__.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **purification** of organic compounds is necessary, though complex, step after its extraction from a natural source or synthesis in the laboratory. 
 
• The method of purification of the organic compound depends mainly on the **nature of the compound and the impurities present**.
 
• The important methods for the separation and purification of organic compounds are Crystallization, Sublimation, Distillation, Differential extraction, and chromatography.
 
• 
 
One easy method to check the purity of an organic compound is to **either melt or boil** it as organic compounds tend to have **sharp melting and boilin**g points. Purification means the removal of **unwanted impurities** present in an organic compound.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some solids can directly pass to the vapour state without going through the liquid phase. The purification technique which exploits this property is called **sublimation**. It is helpful in separating sublimable compounds from non-sublimable ones.
 
• The principle in **crystallization** is that the compound and the impurities have different solubilities in a solvent. A solvent is chosen where the compound to be purified is sparingly soluble, that is, it is sparingly soluble at a lower temperature and soluble at a higher temperature. The solution is heated to get a saturated solution, and on cooling, the crystals of the compounds are removed via filtration.
 
• The underlying principle behind **distillation** is that the mixture of liquids can be separated by the difference in their boiling points. The boiling point is defined as the temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the atmospheric pressure. This method separates volatile liquids from non-volatile liquids.

questions.question: Where is the Green Park Stadium located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Green Park Stadium is a **32,000-capacity** floodlit multi-purpose stadium located in **Kanpur**, **India**, and the Uttar Pradesh cricket team. 
 
• The stadium is under the control of the **Sports Department of Uttar Pradesh**. 
 
• It is the only international cricket stadium in Uttar Pradesh that has regularly hosted international cricket matches in both **Test and One Day formats**. 
 
• The stadium hosted the **500th** test played by the Indian team.
 
• The ground has hosted more than **35 international games** and was also host to India's** 500th Test match**. 
 
• It also has **video screens** that are used during international matches. 
 
• India's first Test win over **Australia** in December **1959** was at the Green Park ground. This was also the **first** match to be played on a** turf wicket** here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uttar Pradesh's chief minister is **Yogi Adityanath.**
 
• The capital of Uttar Pradesh is **Lucknow**.
 
• **Dr.** **Mansukh Mandaviya** is the current Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• There are 6 trophies related to cricket: **Ranji Trophy, the Duleep Trophy, the Vijay Hazare Trophy, the Deodhar Trophy, the Irani Trophy, and the NKP Salve Challenger Trophy**.

questions.question: ‘Revenue Stamp: An Autobiography’ is written by which of the following Indian poets, who was a prominent figure of Punjabi literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrita Pritam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Revenue Stamp: An Autobiography**" is written by **Amrita** **Pritam**.
 
• **Amrita Pritam** was an Indian novelist, essayist, and poet, who wrote in Punjabi and Hindi.
 
• A prominent figure in Punjabi literature, she is the recipient of the **1956 Sahitya Akademi Award**.
 
• Her body of work comprised over **100 books** of poetry, fiction, biographies, essays, a collection of Punjabi folk songs, and an autobiography that were all translated into several Indian and foreign languages.
 
• Pritam is best remembered for her poignant poem, **Ajj aakhaan Waris Shah nu,** an elegy to the 18th-century Punjabi poet, an expression of her anguish over massacres during the partition of India.
 
• As a novelist, her most noted work was **Pinjar** in which she created her memorable character, **Puro**, an epitome of violence against women, loss of humanity, and ultimate surrender to existential fate; the novel was made into an award-winning film, **Pinjar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Behind the name of **Amrita Pritam's** autobiography is the exchange between Amrita and the famous author and journalist, Khushwant Singh, who told her that her life was of so little consequence that it could be written on the back of a revenue stamp.
 
• When choosing the name for her autobiography, Amrita recalled this banter and opted for this name. Credit must be given to the English translator, Krishna Gorowara, who seems to have picked up on all the nuances and depth of Amrita’s thoughts.
 
• The book touches on her life with Imroz, a painter with whom she has a live-in-relationship at a time when such things were far from the norm. Her early marriage to Pritam Singh ends in a divorce. The reasons for their parting and how it affects their two children are covered.

questions.question: Falguni Pathak is a renowned singer known for which of the following genres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarati folk songs**__.

__
 
• Popularly known as the “**Queen of Dandiya**“, **Falguni** **Pathak** is famous for singing traditional music forms of **Gujarat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Falguni Pathak** is an Indian singer, performing artist, and composer based in Mumbai.
 
• Her music is based on traditional musical forms from the Indian state of **Gujarat**.
 
• Her debut album was released in **1998**, and she has also recorded numerous songs for **Bollywood movies**.
 
• The theme of most of her songs is **love**.
 
• She has performed in many shows in India and other countries, backed by a band called **Tha Thaiyaa.**
 
• She has some very popular **Indian pop singles** to her credit, still heard and appreciated all over India.
 
• Her albums are not only famous for the melodious songs but also for the cute love stories depicted in them.
 
• She is very popular in the **Gujarati** community where she is called to perform for popular festivals like **Navaratri**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India **is a geographically and traditionally diverse country.
 
• There are **28** **states** and **8 Union Territories** (U.T.) bonded under the spirit of nationalism.
 
• There are several differences between **Classical music** and **folk music**.
 
• Classical music follows the rules laid in the** Natya Shastra** and cultivates the **Guru-Shisya** tradition whereas folk music tradition is the music that has no hard rules.
 
• **Folk music** is primarily based on diverse themes and is full of brisk rhythm.
 
• They are also set on beats so they can be **dance-oriented**.

questions.question: Guru Bipin Singh was a _________ dancer awarded with Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Guru Bipin Singh was a **Manipuri** dancer awarded with Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966. 
 
• **Guru Bipin Singh** was a director, choreographer, and teacher of Manipuri dance.
 
• He was born on** 23 August 1918** into a Bishnupriya Manipuri Family.
 
• He is regarded as the **Father of Manipuri Dance**.
 
• He choreographed many dance dramas and solo dances and produced many students.
 
• Guru Bipin Singh won many awards such as : 
 
 
• Title of Hanjaba by the Maharaja of Manipur
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi Award,1966
 
• The Sharangdev fellowship by Sur Shringar Samsad
 
• Kalidas Samman by Madhya Pradesh Government
 
• Anamika Kala Sangam award, Kolkata
 
• Shiromani Puraskar by Asian Paints, Kolkata
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Sahitya Akademi Award** is a literary honour in India, which the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters, annually confers on writers of the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the **24 major Indian languages** such as **Telugu, Kannada, Hindi, Tamil, English, Bengali, Punjabi,** and the **22 listed languages** in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution recognised by the Sahitya Akademi, New Delhi.
 
• Established in **1954**, the award comprises a plaque and a cash prize of **₹** **1,00,000**.
 
• The award's purpose is to recognise and promote excellence in **Indian writing and also acknowledge new trends**.
 
• The annual process of selecting awardees runs for the preceding **twelve months**.
 
• The plaque awarded by the Sahitya Akademi was designed by the Indian filmmaker **Satyajit** **Ray**.
